title: pvQuadricClustering
body:
## pvQuadricClustering

Simplifies a polygonal surface by spatial binning: the bounding box is divided into NumberofDimensions bins, all points in a bin collapse to one representative point chosen to minimize quadric error, and degenerate triangles are dropped. It is fast enough for huge meshes (ParaView uses it for level-of-detail rendering), but the result follows the bin grid rather than surface features. Use pvDecimate or decimate when shape fidelity matters more than speed.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Detail smaller than one bin is lost, including thin walls and small holes; increase the divisions on the relevant axis.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `QuadricClustering`. Identity: `filters/QuadricClustering`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

| Port | Meaning / native port | Required | Multiplicity | Kind | Contract |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Input` | Required data input for the native Input port. Give the name of the upstream node to connect, or a {node, port} object to use another of its output ports. ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Quadric Clustering filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CopyCellData` | If this property is set to 1, the cell data from the input will be copied to the output. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `NumberofDimensions` | This property specifies the number of bins along the X, Y, and Z axes of the data set. | `{"items":{"type":"integer"},"maxItems":3,"minItems":3,"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `[1,1,1]` |
| `UseFeatureEdges` | If this property is set to 1, feature edge quadrics will be used to maintain the boundary edges along processor divisions. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseFeaturePoints` | If this property is set to 1, feature point quadrics will be used to maintain the boundary points along processor divisions. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseInputPoints` | If the value of this property is set to 1, the representative point for each bin is selected from one of the input points that lies in that bin; the input point that produces the least error is chosen. If the value of this property is 0, the location of the representative point is calculated to produce the least error possible for that bin, but the point will most likely not be one of the input points. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `UseInternalTriangles` | If this property is set to 1, triangles completely contained in a spatial bin will be included in the computation of the bin's quadrics. When this property is set to 0, the filters operates faster, but the resulting surface may not be as well-behaved. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
